checklist.item: Coping or cap slopes back to the roof side and has a drip edge clear of both wall faces.
checklist.why: A flat or outward-sloping cap holds water and stains or wets the facade.

checklist.item: Roof membrane base flashing turns up the parapet at least 8 in (200 mm) above the finished roof surface and is terminated and counter-flashed.
checklist.why: Low or unterminated base flashing is the most common parapet leak.

checklist.item: A continuous membrane or sheet-metal underlayment runs over the top of the parapet, under the coping, lapped onto both faces.
checklist.why: Coping joints leak; the layer below is what keeps water out of the wall.

checklist.item: Air and water barrier of the wall is shown continuous with the roof membrane across the parapet.
checklist.why: A break here lets interior air into the parapet, where it condenses.

checklist.item: Continuous insulation wraps the parapet or the thermal break at the roof-to-wall line is shown; R-value meets the energy code for the project climate zone.
checklist.why: An uninsulated parapet is a thermal bridge around the whole roof.

checklist.item: Cant or tapered edge, fastening of the coping (continuous cleat) and the wood blocking are labelled, with a scale and material tags.
checklist.why: The builder needs these to price and build it; missing labels become RFIs.
